name: inference-hud
description: Live tokens/sec, token counts, and time-to-first-token for local inference servers, in the status bar.
author: Charles Nutter

commands.title: Inference HUD: Set Up Local Model

inferenceHud.endpoints.markdownDescription:
Inference servers to watch, as base URLs. The engine at each is detected automatically.

Usually you need none of these: supported engines on well-known localhost ports are found on their own. Add one for a non-default port or a server on another machine.

To pin an engine or run a proxy on a chosen port, use `#inferenceHud.endpointOverrides#`.

[▶ Set up a local model](command:inferenceHud.setupModel)

inferenceHud.autoDetect.markdownDescription: Scan well-known ports on `127.0.0.1` for supported engines and watch whatever is found. Only localhost is ever scanned; remote servers must be listed in `#inferenceHud.endpoints#`.

inferenceHud.autoProxy.markdownDescription:
Automatically proxy detected engines that publish no server-wide telemetry, such as Ollama and LM Studio. Without this they cannot be measured at all; with it, the extension listens on a local port and forwards to the engine, reading the stream as it passes. You still point your client's base URL at the proxy — run `Inference HUD: Set Up Local Model` to do that without editing JSON.

Off by default because it opens a listening socket on `127.0.0.1`.

[▶ Set up a local model](command:inferenceHud.setupModel)

inferenceHud.autoProxyPort.markdownDescription: First port an automatically started proxy may claim. Further engines take the next free port up. Ports named explicitly in `#inferenceHud.endpoints#` are never reused.

inferenceHud.endpointOverrides.markdownDescription:
Endpoints needing more than a URL. Rarely required.

```json
[
  { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:9090", "engine": "llamacpp" },
  { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:11434", "proxy": 8788 }
]
```

`engine` pins detection; `proxy` listens on that port and forwards to `url`, which is how engines publishing no telemetry are measured. `#inferenceHud.autoProxy#` does the latter for you.

engine.description: Pin the engine instead of detecting it.

proxy.description: Listen on this port and forward to url, measuring traffic as it passes.

inferenceHud.statusBarPriority.description: Status bar item priority (higher is further left).

walkthroughs.title: Measure your local models
walkthroughs.description: Put tokens/sec, token counts and time-to-first-token in the status bar, for whichever local engine you use.

steps.title: Start a local inference server
steps.description:
Inference HUD watches the server, not the editor, so any client's traffic moves it — including GitHub Copilot's agent mode.

Start whichever engine you use. Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, MTPLX and LM Studio on their usual localhost ports are all found without configuration.
[Check what was found](command:inferenceHud.showLog)

media.altText: Detected engines listed in the log

steps.title: Turn on measurement for engines that publish nothing
steps.description:
Ollama, LM Studio and LocalAI report their timings only to whoever made the request, so they cannot be watched from outside. Measuring them means routing their traffic through the extension.

Skip this if you only use llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang or MTPLX — those publish telemetry directly and need nothing.
[Enable proxying](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22inferenceHud.autoProxy%22)

steps.title: Add your models to the chat picker
steps.description:
Optional, and only for driving your local model from Copilot Chat. The status bar works regardless of which client sends the traffic.

This reads the models your server actually has and builds the entry for you, pointed at the right URL.
[Set up a local model](command:inferenceHud.setupModel)
